Choosing care

How to Choose a Counselor

Finding the right counselor involves more than picking the first available name. Training, experience, approach, accessibility, cost, and how comfortable you feel asking questions can all matter.

Last updated September 19, 2026 · Editorial policy

Start with your priorities

Think about the main concern you want help with, whether you prefer in-person or telehealth sessions, insurance or budget needs, schedule, location, and any preferences around treatment approach or provider characteristics.

Questions for an initial consultation

  • What experience do you have with this concern?
  • What approaches do you commonly use?
  • How do you measure whether therapy is helping?
  • What are your fees, insurance policies, and cancellation rules?
  • How do you handle urgent situations between sessions?

Fit can take more than one conversation

A therapist can be well qualified and still not feel like the right match. It is reasonable to ask questions, discuss concerns about the process, or choose a different provider when the fit is not working.

Looking for local support?

Use the counselor directory to compare providers by specialty, approach, location, insurance, availability, and visit type.
